hints: Focus on what actually makes the glass dark, silver atoms ($\text{Ag}$), and track when $\text{Ag}$ is made or used up.
Check oxidation numbers in reactions 2 and 3 to see what happens to $\text{Cu}^+$ and $\text{Cu}^{2+}$, who is oxidised and who is reduced.
Add reactions 2 and 3 together and cancel species that appear on both sides to see if copper is used up overall or regenerated.
walkthrough:
**Link darkness to silver atoms**

Remember the stem tells you darkness is due to $\text{Ag}$ atoms, not $\text{Ag}^+$ ions. So making $\text{Ag}$ darkens, removing $\text{Ag}$ lightens.

$$\text{Ag}^+ + \text{Cl}^- \rightleftharpoons \text{Ag} + \text{Cl} \quad \text{(reaction 1)}$$

**Assign oxidation and reduction in reactions 2 and 3**

In reaction 2, $\text{Cu}^+$ becomes $\text{Cu}^{2+}$. That is loss of electrons, so oxidation. $\text{Cu}^+$ is the reducing agent, and $\text{Cl}$ becomes $\text{Cl}^-$ by gaining an electron.

$$\text{Cu}^+ + \text{Cl} \rightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+} + \text{Cl}^-$$

**Check reaction 3 the same way**

In reaction 3, $\text{Ag}$ becomes $\text{Ag}^+$. That is also loss of electrons, so $\text{Ag}$ is oxidised. $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ becomes $\text{Cu}^+$ by gaining an electron, so it is reduced.

$$\text{Cu}^{2+} + \text{Ag} \rightarrow \text{Cu}^+ + \text{Ag}^+$$

**Spot the catalyst cycle**

Now add reactions 2 and 3 and cancel. $\text{Cu}^+$ is used in 2 and remade in 3, $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ is made in 2 and used in 3. Neither is used up overall.

$$\text{Cl} + \text{Ag} \rightarrow \text{Cl}^- + \text{Ag}^+$$

**Conclude the correct statement**

That overall change is just the reverse of reaction 1, removing $\text{Ag}$ atoms so the glass lightens. Because copper ions are regenerated unchanged while speeding up this reversal, they act as catalysts.

options.A: Correct. Cu+ is consumed in reaction 2 and regenerated in reaction 3, while Cu2+ is formed in reaction 2 and consumed in reaction 3. They take part but are not used up overall, which is the classic test for catalysis.
options.B: False. An oxidising agent is itself reduced. In reaction 2, Cu+ to Cu2+ is oxidation (increase in oxidation number from +1 to +2), so Cu+ is the reducing agent, not the oxidising agent. The Cl atom is the oxidising agent here.
options.C: False. Reaction 3 converts Ag atoms into Ag+ ions. Since darkness is caused by Ag atoms, using them up decreases darkness and makes the glass more transparent, the opposite of what is stated.
options.D: False. In reaction 3, Ag changes to Ag+, losing one electron. Loss of electrons is oxidation, so silver atoms are oxidised, not reduced. Cu2+ is the species reduced to Cu+.
